claims.text: SECTION 2a PROVENANCE. HE WAS GIVEN THE OTHER WITNESS'S FRAME ON THE RECORDED CALL. The interviewer withheld it and said so on air, telling Johnson nothing about November-5 and nothing about a UFO. Mario Woods was then patched in and within two minutes supplied the site and date, the vacation-relief detail, and then the category: asked at 00:07:29 whether he remembered what they encountered at 0100, Johnson answered 'No' at 00:07:35; Woods then asked twice whether it was a UFO; Johnson assented after a pause at 00:07:46; Woods then asked how far over the top of the blaster it was and Johnson gave 'under 50 feet'.

claims.text: THE EPISODE'S OWN RETELLING OF THAT MOMENT DIVERGES FROM ITS OWN RECORDING OF IT. At 00:17:46-00:18:11, with Johnson present, the recognition is recounted as Woods naming only the year, base and site and Johnson immediately saying 'Oh, that UFO', with the producer characterising it as chilling because no other details were supplied. The recorded call at 00:07:29-00:07:46 shows an initial 'No', then Woods naming the UFO, then assent. Both passages are timestamped in the same episode.

claims.text: SECTION 2a PROVENANCE. WHERE THE ACCOUNTS DIVERGE IS THE STRONGEST THING IN HIS FAVOUR. They agree on substance, an object above the site, figures, missing time and separate interrogation, and they diverge sharply on posture and agency: Johnson's account is passive throughout, frozen to the steering wheel, unable to speak or blink, hearing Woods shouting, while Woods's is active, out of the truck and calling Johnson to come and look. Agreement on substance with divergence on detail reads very differently from verbatim agreement.

label: Michael Johnson
narrative: Michael Johnson is on this board because CLAUDE.md section 2a admits him and because excluding him would destroy the most instructive provenance record in the file. He is presented as the second man at Launch Facility November-5 on 18 November 1977, missing for forty-nine years and found in June 2026. HOW HE WAS FOUND IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT MUST TRAVEL WITH THE CLAIM. He was located not by the original witness, not by a records search and not by AARO, but by the party publishing the result: a viewer of the show sent the production a Facebook page belonging to a Michael Johnson in his seventies in South Carolina, and an unnamed recruiter tasked by the producer found him in about a week. The first contact call is dated on air to 26 June 2026. NO DATED PUBLIC STATEMENT BY MICHAEL JOHNSON ABOUT THIS EVENT EXISTS PRIOR TO THAT CALL. The only pre-contact artefact identified in a two hour forty-seven minute episode is an undated Facebook post placing him at Ellsworth in the right years and saying nothing whatever about the event. Two further things must be held together rather than traded off. The interviewer ran a deliberate blind-contact protocol and told Johnson nothing about November-5 or a UFO, and should be credited for it. And within ninety seconds of being patched in, the original witness supplied the site, the date, the category and the altitude frame, and Johnson answered 'No' when first asked what they encountered before assenting after the UFO was named for him. The episode's own later on-camera retelling of that moment says Johnson recognised it immediately with nothing supplied; the recording of the call does not show that. The two accounts agree on substance and diverge on posture and agency, Johnson's being passive throughout and Woods's active, which reads very differently from verbatim agreement and is the strongest thing in Johnson's favour.
